audits.title: 898 The Fragility Fracture Post-Operative Mobilisation (FFPOM) Study – a UK-Wide Audit of Lower-Limb Fragility Fractures

cycle1.result: Immediate weight-bearing allowed in 15543 (95.7%) hip fracture and 1071 (32.3%) non-hip fracture patients; unrestricted weight-bearing after femoral shaft 47.8% and distal femur 64.6% fixation.

audits.other_findings: 45.6% of distal femur and 44.2% of femoral shaft fractures were periprosthetic vs 2.2% of proximal femur; foot and ankle was the commonest non-hip fracture (45.1%).
audits.citation: Zargaran A, Bretherton C, Richardson C, Raza M, Eardley W, Trompeter A. 898 The Fragility Fracture Post-Operative Mobilisation (FFPOM) Study – a UK-Wide Audit of Lower-Limb Fragility Fractures. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac268.054.

audits.title: 1100 Fragility Fractures Post-Operative Mobilisation - A Major Trauma Centre Audit
audits.standard: BOAST: surgery in frail patients should allow full weight-bearing and be performed within 36 hours of admission
audits.setting: Major Trauma Centre, Royal Stoke University Hospital

cycle1.result: 146 (93%) allowed full weight-bearing: 133 (98.5%) hip fractures and 12 (54.5%) non-hip fractures.

audits.other_findings: Mean restricted weight bearing 42 days (range 28 to 56); authors suggest routine frailty assessment.

audits.title: 100 Weightbearing Status Documentation in Orthopaedic Operation Notes – A Snapshot Audit
audits.standard: BOAST guidance on weight-bearing terminology and documentation; target 80% compliance
audits.setting: Single centre, lower-limb operation notes (trauma and elective), Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 6% compliance (non-weightbearing cases only); no rationale given for limited or non-weightbearing status; functional and duration limitations given in 60% and 86% respectively.

audits.intervention: After consultation with physiotherapists: theatre posters, template training and reminder messages via WhatsApp groups for surgeons.
audits.other_findings: Significant variability in terminology; rapid-cycle re-audits are under way.
audits.citation: Patel M, Tulloch A, Khaleeq T, Theivendran K. 100 Weightbearing Status Documentation in Orthopaedic Operation Notes – A Snapshot Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.213.

audits.title: 997 An Audit into Compliance with Boast Standards for Mobilisation and Weightbearing After Orthopaedic Surgery
audits.standard: BOAST standards for documentation of mobilisation and weightbearing after orthopaedic surgery

cycle1.result: 11 operation notes compliant; lower limb (excluding NOF) 14% (7/50), upper limb 7% (4/59), neck of femur 0% (0/50).

audits.intervention: Suggested reformatting of the operation note and education (not yet done).
audits.other_findings: All but one NOF note ticked 'full weightbearing' rather than the new term 'unrestricted weightbearing'.

audits.title: The Fragility Fracture Postoperative Mobilisation multicentre audit : the reality of weightbearing practices following operations for lower limb fragility fractures.
audits.standard: British Orthopaedic Association Standard: all surgery in the frail patient should allow full weightbearing for activities required for daily living
audits.setting: Multicentre audit in publicly funded health services (FFPOM)

cycle1.period: 1 January 2019 to 30 June 2019, and 1 February 2021 to 14 March 2021
cycle1.result: 16,614 (85.0%) instructed to weightbear for daily living immediately postoperatively: 15,543 (95.7%) hip fracture and 1,071 (32.3%) non-hip fracture patients.

audits.other_findings: Median length of stay 12.2 days (IQR 7.9 to 20.0); shaft and distal femur fractures had longer stays than similar hip fracture patients.
audits.citation: Richardson C, Bretherton CP, Raza M, Zargaran A, Eardley WGP, Trompeter AJ, et al.. The Fragility Fracture Postoperative Mobilisation multicentre audit : the reality of weightbearing practices following operations for lower limb fragility fractures. audits.title: Weight-Bearing Status After Peri-Prosthetic Proximal Femur Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation (ORIF) or Revision Arthroplasty: A Clinical Audit.
audits.standard: British Hip Society guidance: aim for full weight-bearing in the immediate postoperative period; no target stated
audits.setting: Dorset County Hospital, district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics; data from the Hip Fracture Registry

cycle1.result: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).

audits.intervention: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.
audits.other_findings: Limited and non-weight-bearing instructions often lacked specific functional restrictions and duration, making rehabilitation difficult. The single fixation failure occurred in a patient allowed full weight-bearing.
audits.citation: Mitchell O, Ward P, Petrov K. Weight-Bearing Status After Peri-Prosthetic Proximal Femur Fracture Open Reduction and Internal Fixation (ORIF) or Revision Arthroplasty: A Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2025;17(8):e90805. doi:10.7759/cureus.90805. PMID: 40995306.

audits.title: Early Weight-Bearing Following Ankle Fixation in a United Kingdom Major Trauma Centre: Real-World Adoption Versus a Contemporary Randomised Trial and British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma.
audits.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance (weight-bearing as tolerated after stable fixation) and WAX trial (weight-bearing from two weeks)

cycle1.result: First weight-bearing at 2 weeks 2/42 (4.8%), 2–6 weeks 9/42 (21.4%), over 6 weeks 31/42 (73.8%) (6–8 weeks 21/42, 50.0%; over 8 weeks 10/42, 23.8%). Median 48 days (IQR 42–56); none discharged weight-bearing as tolerated.

audits.other_findings: Early safety was reassuring (unplanned contact 1/42, no re-operations or loss of reduction, delayed union 2/42). Posterior malleolus fixation was linked to longer time to weight-bearing (p=0.036); re-audit planned at 6–9 months after a default WBAT-from-two-weeks pathway.
audits.citation: Al-Hano H, Beech Z. Early Weight-Bearing Following Ankle Fixation in a United Kingdom Major Trauma Centre: Real-World Adoption Versus a Contemporary Randomised Trial and British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97076. doi:10.7759/cureus.97076. PMID: 41416288.

audits.title: Management of Fragility Femoral Fractures: A UK Regional Multicentre Audit of the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST 'The care of the older or frail orthopaedic trauma patient' (2019) point 14: all surgery in the frail patient should allow full weight bearing and be performed within 36 hours of admission
audits.setting: Seven NHS hospitals in the Wessex Deanery (Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole, Salisbury, Basingstoke, Dorchester, Isle of Wight); multicentre retrospective audit

cycle1.result: Of 342 patients with time-to-surgery data, 86 (25%) had surgery within 36 hours; 256 had surgery after 36 hours. FWB prescribed in 41 (76%) arthroplasty vs 173 (57%) fixation patients; arthroplasty patients breached 36 hours more often (n = 46, 85%) than fixation (n = 218, 72%).

audits.other_findings: Fixation (n = 303, 85%) was the main treatment; FWB was achieved by 36 (87%) arthroplasty vs 121 (70%) fixation patients prescribed it. Median length of stay was 13 days with surgery within 36 hours vs 17 days after, and NWB patients were less often discharged home (21% vs 56% FWB).
audits.citation: Ormiston R, Pearce K, Hancock D, Kondi S, Abdellatif A, White S, et al.. Management of Fragility Femoral Fractures: A UK Regional Multicentre Audit of the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e109830. doi:10.7759/cureus.109830. PMID: 42367434.
